questions.question: Which InterSystems IRIS mechanism is responsible for preventing database corruption if a system crash occurs while modified database blocks are being written to disk?
questions.explanation: T4.3 — The Write Image Journal (WIJ) stores a copy of modified database blocks before they are written to the actual database file, ensuring structural integrity upon crash recovery.

questions.question: You initiate a transaction using TSTART. During the transaction, you update a global that resides in a database where Journaling is explicitly set to 'No'. You then issue a TROLLBACK command. What happens to the global?

options.text: The global is rolled back to its state prior to TSTART.
The TROLLBACK command throws an exception.
The global is NOT rolled back; the changes remain.
The entire database is marked as read-only.

questions.explanation: T4.3 — Rollback operations rely entirely on Transaction Journaling. If journaling is disabled for a database, changes to its globals cannot be rolled back.

questions.question: After a hardware failure destroys your primary database disk, you restore a backup from yesterday. Which mechanism allows you to recover the transactions made between the backup time and the crash?
questions.explanation: T4.3 — Transaction Journal files record the logical changes made to data over time, allowing you to replay them forward against a restored backup.
